clue.text: Small lock causing tension

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: A tiny curl of hair seems to be at the root of somebody's nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress and tension are synonyms for mental or physical strain.

clue.text: Take off from PSV going over country

indicators.note: going over turns the vehicle upside down, read upwards in a down entry

parts.note: PSV is a public service vehicle, such as a bus
a tract is a stretch of country or land

explanation.surface: Someone removes things from a bus as it travels across the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to deduct, to take one quantity away from another.

clue.text: Negotiated rise expected remains

indicators.note: a negotiated deal is reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: due means expected, as in a train due at noon

explanation.surface: An agreed pay rise is still anticipated.
explanation.definitionFit: Residue is what is left over, the remainder.

clue.text: Sir Roger criticises being put up — here?

definitions.text: Sir Roger criticises being put up — here?

indicators.note: put up means written upwards in this down entry

parts.note: Sir Roger Moore was the actor who played James Bond
raps means criticises sharply

explanation.surface: Is this where Roger Moore grumbles about being made to stay as a guest?
explanation.walkthrough: 'being put up' reverses MOORE RAPS into SPAR EROOM; it also means being given a bed, which is where a guest would be.
explanation.definitionFit: A spare room is a guest bedroom, where visitors are put up.

clue.text: Precipitate from a Jersey evacuation?

parts.note: Jersey is one of the Channel Islands, abbreviated CI
to drain something is to empty it, so a drain is an evacuation

explanation.surface: Asks what comes out of an emptying on the island of Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precipitate' is a noun here: rain, snow and the like that falls from the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain is polluted rainfall, a kind of atmospheric precipitation.

clue.text: Daily performance controversial in nature? Typical!

parts.note: a daily is a cleaner who comes in every day, also called a char
an act is a performance
eristic describes argument for its own sake, disputatious

explanation.surface: The cleaner's show stirs up argument, which is no surprise at all.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'daily' or 'char' is a British term for a domestic cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Something characteristic is typical of a person or thing.

clue.text: Speech by Texan, say, upset minor learner

indicators.note: upset means overturned, read upwards in this down entry

parts.note: a ward is a minor in the care of a guardian
L is a learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A Texan's talk unsettled a young student.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a slow, drawn-out way of speaking, typical of the American South.

clue.text: Dire commercial jingle

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a jingle is a short piece of verse

explanation.surface: An advertising jingle that is truly awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse conditions are unfavourable, bad or harmful.

clue.text: Partners accepting only twisted leggings?

indicators.note: the partners take the rearranged word inside

parts.note: North and South are partners in bridge

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of only are rearranged

explanation.surface: A couple accept nothing but tights that have got all tangled.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are stockings, which cover the legs; the query flags the loose fit.

clue.text: Fellow artist initially idly drew ducks and crow

parts.note: cock is an old familiar term for a fellow

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of artist

parts.note: to doodle is to draw idly
a duck is zero in cricket, written O, so two make OO

explanation.surface: A painter sketches waterfowl and a black bird without much thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crow' is the verb's noun, the rooster's call, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock-a-doodle-doo is the cry of a rooster, its crow.

clue.text: Leading man — a star that's seen on the dance floor

definitions.text: that's seen on the dance floor

parts.note: the boss is the man in charge, the one who leads
a nova is a star that suddenly flares in brightness

explanation.surface: A film's leading man is a star, recognisable when he dances.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian dance style, so it is performed in ballrooms.

clue.text: Part of forge in Roman villa

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words Roman villa, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's workshop component found in an ancient Roman house.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the iron block a smith hammers metal on in a smithy.

clue.text: Narrow-minded communist with audacity

parts.note: red is the colour and nickname of communists
neck is British slang for cheek or nerve

explanation.surface: A bigoted leftist with plenty of nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Redneck, used as an adjective, describes bigoted, reactionary attitudes.

clue.text: Prison warden losing head — nothing new in section of wing

indicators.note: the warden loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a jailer guards a prison
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A beheaded jailer and an empty novelty somehow end up in an aircraft's wing.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is the hinged flap on an aircraft's wing that controls roll.

clue.text: The beliefs of company Leftist embraced

indicators.note: the company holds the leftist inside it, as in an embrace

parts.note: a red is a left-winger

explanation.surface: A firm's articles of faith turn out to include a socialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of a person's or group's beliefs, a creed.

clue.text: Redrafted letter after party flyer

indicators.note: the rearranged word comes after the party word

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: a redrafted text has been rewritten, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A letter rewritten after a celebration gets turned into a leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' looks like a printed handbill; it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The dotterel is a small plover, a bird, and so a creature that flies.

clue.text: Meet stern eccentric getting something to eat

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters are rearranged oddly

explanation.surface: A strict, odd character is encountered while getting a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Entremets are side dishes or desserts served between courses.

clue.text: I can't see flicks. That's tricky for me!

definitions.text: I can't see flicks. That's tricky for me!

indicators.note: tricky signals the letters of I can't see are mixed up

explanation.surface: A film buff laments being unable to watch films.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges I CANT SEE; a film lover would indeed find not seeing films hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A cineaste is a devotee of cinema, a film enthusiast.

clue.text: Record mostly minor changes in style of movie

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter dropped

parts.note: to file something is to record it

indicators.note: changes signals the letters of minor are rearranged

explanation.surface: An archive noting small amendments to how a film looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts FILE to FIL; 'changes' turns MINOR into MNOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Film noir is a genre of dark, cynical crime cinema from the 1940s and 50s.

clue.text: Pressing chore

explanation.definitionFit: Ironing is both smoothing clothes with a hot iron and a typical domestic job.

clue.text: Returning, achieved very good times

indicators.note: returning means the word met is read backwards

parts.note: to meet a target is to achieve it, so met = achieved
pi is slang for pious, very good

explanation.surface: Coming back, someone scored excellent results.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi is the plural of tempo, the speed of a piece of music, its time.

clue.text: Macbeth's query about his status, it would seem, is a gas

parts.note: Macbeth asking about himself would say me

parts.words: about his status, it would seem
parts.note: Macbeth was Thane of Glamis, so his rank is thane

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Scottish lord wonders about his rank, which turns out to be hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'Me, thane?', the question Macbeth might ask on hearing his titles.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is a flammable hydrocarbon, the main component of natural gas.

clue.text: Bow of sailing boat in outline

indicators.note: the bow is a vessel's front, so the first letter of sailing

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: The front of a sailing vessel shown in silhouette.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing or summary, a basic outline.

clue.text: Cocky type rounded hill, was almost captured

indicators.note: the hill holds the shortened word inside it, as if captured

parts.note: a knoll is a small rounded hill

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A conceited person on a round hill was nearly taken prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all is a person who arrogantly thinks they know everything.

clue.text: Irish missionary — top judo expert?

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, top, with the 1 read as I
a dan is a grade of black belt in judo, and a holder of it

explanation.surface: Is a missionary from Ireland also a first-class martial artist?
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Aidan was an Irish monk who founded Lindisfarne and evangelised Northumbria.

clue.text: Small collie that may be ordered to 'Heel' and 'Sit'!

indicators.note: the two command words are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A little sheepdog being given the usual obedience commands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' reads as a dog being commanded, but it is the anagram signal on the two quoted commands.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheltie is the common name for the Shetland sheepdog, a miniature collie breed.

clue.text: Eastern criminals — one into jazz

indicators.note: the numeral goes into the jazz word

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Gangsters from the East, one of them a jazz fan.
explanation.definitionFit: Triads are Chinese organised-crime gangs, comparable to the Mafia.

clue.text: Carts taking in poor view in approaches to manor-houses

indicators.note: the carts word contains the rearranged letters

parts.note: drays are heavy carts, used for beer barrels

indicators.note: poor signals the letters of view are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Wagons obscure the view along the roads up to country estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' is the anagram signal and 'taking in' puts the rearranged letters inside the carts.
explanation.definitionFit: A driveway is the private road leading up to a large house.

clue.text: Western peak attracting almost nobody

parts.note: a peak is a high point, so high

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter

parts.note: no one means nobody

explanation.surface: A cowboy film's summit draws hardly any visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' is the noun: a cowboy film.
explanation.definitionFit: High Noon is a classic 1952 cowboy film starring Gary Cooper.

clue.text: Ancient Jew from German city quarter

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr, Germany
E (east) is one of the four compass quarters

explanation.surface: An ancient Hebrew man came from part of a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect of the Second Temple period.
